The 30-minute lesson on O3 is written, with a quiz and key to go with it. I haven't opened the lesson in a browser, counted its words, or checked its links. I estimate it at about 4,000 words, inside the 2,700–6,750 range for 30 minutes. Its external links came from this session's searches and page fetches.

**Lesson:** `lessons/0001-context-and-memory-in-an-agent.html`

It uses the makerspace assistant throughout and covers:
- **Context window:** what is in the context on one call, and what a token is.
- **Between steps:** the model keeps nothing between calls, and the program re-sends the history each time. A worked example counts the input tokens across a run, so you can see cost grow.
- **When it fills:** context rot, and clearing old tool results, trimming and compaction.
- **Between sessions:** saved notes as memory, with a student-record example.
- **Retrieval:** searching the manuals for a few chunks instead of pasting them in, and the choice between loading up front or on demand.

It has three figures, a check after each section, a sorting exercise you do yourself, and a summary. The main source is Anthropic's [Effective context engineering for AI agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents). The others are the [Claude context windows docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows) and the [LangChain memory docs](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/concepts/memory). I only saw the LangChain page in search results and did not open it.

**Quiz:** `quizzes/0002.json`, with five items and its key in `keys/0002.json`. It is ready when you want it. I've given no answers here.

**Also written:**
- A cheat sheet at `cheatsheets/context-and-memory.html`.
- `RESOURCES.md`, listing those three sources.
- `assets/lesson.css` and `assets/lesson.js`, which later lessons will share.
- Updated `NOTES.md`, which records three shared misconception ids (M1 to M3) used in the key.

Quiz 0001 is still ungraded (both attempts).

Ask me anything in the chat about any part of the lesson. I also couldn't find a trusted community link to recommend. Would you like to name one, or should I suggest some next time?
